item.title: Foreign Ministry Spokesperson Guo Jiakun’s Regular Press Conference on September 10, 2026
item.description:
Published: 2026-09-10
AFP: Will Chinese leader travel to India this weekend for the BRICS Summit? Guo Jiakun: On this question, I have no information to share at the moment. Reuters: India’s Serious Fraud Office has recommended that China’s Xiaomi be investigated for alleged irregularities in its business model and compliance with foreign investment law. Does the foreign ministry have any comment on that? Guo Jiakun: I’m not familiar with the specifics. China-India economic and trade cooperation is mutually beneficial in nature. We hope India will provide a fair, just, transparent and non-discriminatory environment for the investment and operation of companies of all countries in India. NBC: At his meeting with the U.S. Ambassador David Perdue the other week, Foreign Minister Wang Yi urged both sides to “eliminate interference and overcome obstacles” for high-level engagements between the two countries. Is there any example of “obstacle” that the Chinese side believes is within the U.S. ability to tackle or otherwise, in general, are both sides, from their most recent communications, making some progress in dealing with these “obstacles”? Guo Jiakun: China released a readout on Foreign Minister Wang Yi’s meeting with U.S. Ambassador to China David Perdue. Head-of-state diplomacy plays an irreplaceable role in providing strategic guidance to bilateral relations. China and the U.S. are in communication regarding interactions between the two heads of state within the year. Global Times: It is reported that in a media briefing, the U.S. embassy in Panama introduced a pilot AI supply chain credentialing and provenance platform in Panama, the first of its kind in the world. The U.S. said the project was under evaluation. Some media commented that by verifying the origin, custody, and compliance status of cargo for AI infrastructure, semiconductors, and critical minerals, the project in essence serves the U.S. control of tech industrial and supply chains and tech blockade of China. What’s your comment? Guo Jiakun: We noticed relevant reports. The development of AI bears on the common welfare of all humanity. All parties should jointly promote the open and inclusive development of AI for good and for all. Exclusive groupings and geopolitical calculations are not conducive to technological development and progress in LAC countries and the rest of the Global South. China will work with LAC countries and other parties to jointly build a just and equitable global AI governance system, and develop AI for the good of people worldwide. Reuters: Nepal is planning to ask wealthier countries and agencies for financial help this week. It has said that they should contribute to the US$5 billion that’s needed for the rebuilding following the flooding. Has Nepal asked China for financial help and does China have any plans to contribute? Guo Jiakun: After the sudden mudslide struck the China-Nepal border areas, while urgently carrying out rescue and relief efforts at home, China immediately reached out to Nepal to support its emergency response and disaster relief. China and Nepal are traditional friends and close neighbors. We stand ready to assist Nepal in post-disaster reconstruction to the best of our capability based on its needs. We believe the Nepali people will overcome difficulties and rebuild their homes soon under the leadership of their government.

item.title: Foreign Ministry Spokesperson Mao Ning’s Regular Press Conference on September 9, 2026
item.description:
Published: 2026-09-09
Xinhua News Agency: We noted recent comments saying China only cares for its own development while “pulling up the ladder” for the development of other Global South countries. What is your comment? Mao Ning: China never pulls up the ladder from any country. Rather, China has long been building up ladders so that countries could reach higher together. Through high-quality Belt and Road cooperation, for instance, China has been helping partner countries bridge the infrastructure gap. By providing Global South countries with affordable industrial equipment and tech products and sharing experience and expertise, China has helped lower the cost for these countries’ industrial growth. China’s zero-tariff policy and “Export to China” initiative generate profits and market opportunities that enable Global South countries to better integrate into the global supply chains and enhance growth resilience. For China, cooperation with other countries has always been about mutual success. The “pulling-up-the-ladder” narrative has zero resonance with Global South countries. China will always pursue mutual benefit and common development, be a reliable partner of Global South countries, and contribute to the prosperity of the Global South through China’s own development. AFP: U.S. cyber security firm Calif said yesterday that it has built an AI-assisted hacking tool that can access the personal accounts and private information on the Chinese app WeChat. Tencent has said that the security risk has been fixed after being notified by Calif. But as a matter of cyber security, does the foreign ministry have comments on this? Mao Ning: I’m not familiar with the specifics. China stands for promoting AI for good and preventing the abuse and malicious use of AI. AFP: Yesterday, the U.S. Cyber Defense Agency accused top Chinese AI labs, including DeepSeek and Moonshot of stealing the capabilities of U.S. models. It said that these campaigns “form the core” of China-based AI companies’ strategies. Does the foreign ministry have a comment on this? Mao Ning: The development of AI in China comes from greater self-reliance and strength in science and technology, and is fueled by China’s vision of extensive consultation and joint contribution for shared benefit and commitment to open cooperation. We believe all parties need to make sure AI development is open and inclusive and promotes the well-being of humanity as a force for good and for all. We hope the U.S. side will earnestly act on the important common understandings reached between the two presidents and stop leveling false allegations to smear China. As two major powers in AI, China and the U.S. should step up cooperation. NHK: The BRICS Summit will be held in India this weekend. Who will lead the Chinese delegation? Mao Ning: We will release timely information if there is any update. Please stay tuned. AFP: At an international forum yesterday, the Defense Secretary of the Philippines Gilberto Teodoro Jr. criticized what he called a violation of UNCLOS and “coercion, bullying and aggression” by China in response to him being handed a piece of paper stating China’s position on the South China Sea. Does the foreign ministry have a comment on the situation or a response to the remarks by the Philippines’ Defense Secretary? Mao Ning: I’m not sure what exactly happened at the event, but China’s position has always been clear on the so-called “South China Sea arbitration”. The Philippines unilaterally initiated the case, which is a distortion and abuse of the UNCLOS dispute settlement mechanism. It is the Philippine side who has violated UNCLOS and undermined its integrity and authority. We urge the certain individual of the Philippine side to cut the provocations and theatrics, and stop undermining China-Philippines relations and stability in the South China Sea.

item.title: Foreign Ministry Spokesperson Mao Ning’s Regular Press Conference on September 8, 2026
item.description:
Published: 2026-09-08
CCTV: Could you update us on China’s assistance for Nepal’s disaster relief efforts? Mao Ning: To support Nepal’s rescue and relief efforts, China sent out this morning the fourth batch of emergency relief supplies, including equipment for transportation and lighting and mortuary supplies. Across China, help is on the way to Nepal. China Foundation for Rural Development has sent people to the affected communities in Nepal to set up temporary shelters and provide daily necessities and basic medical services. The Chinese Enterprises Association in Nepal recently delivered the first batch of funds donated for relief operations. China will continue standing firmly with Nepal to overcome this challenging time together. RT: The Japanese government recently asked Russia to remove a monument commemorating the victory over Japan’s militarism, saying that this issue affects the feelings of the Japanese people. And Japan also claimed that the “Enemy State Clauses” in the UN Charter are obsolete. How does China view these comments made by the Japanese government on WWII history and postwar international order? Mao Ning: To view and treat history correctly is a key gauge of Japan’s commitment to peaceful development. Japan joined the UN after admitting to its militarist crimes and recognizing the UN Charter in its entirety. The “Enemy State Clauses” in the Charter, a special set of rules for WWII defeated states, are still valid today. This year marks the 80th anniversary of the opening of the Tokyo Trials. The Japanese side should use history as a mirror, make a clean break with militarism, and earn trust from its Asian neighbors and the rest of the world with concrete actions. China-Arab TV: Prime Minister and Minister of Foreign Affairs of Qatar Sheikh Mohammed bin Abdulrahman Al Thani is on a visit to China from September 7 to 8. Can you elaborate on the goals and significance of this visit? Specifically, how does China view the timing of this visit, and what are the outcomes of the bilateral talks? Mao Ning: China and Qatar are strategic partners. China highly values its relations with Qatar. Qatari Prime Minister and Minister of Foreign Affairs Sheikh Mohammed bin Abdulrahman Al Thani is on a visit to China. Yesterday, Premier Li Qiang met with him for in-depth exchange of views on issues of mutual interest. China looks to the visit as an opportunity to work for new progress in bilateral relations. On more details about the visit, we will release timely readouts. Please check back for updates. Beijing Youth Daily: We noted that China is hosting a Workshop on AI Capacity-Building in Beijing. Could you share with us more details? What’s China’s view on AI capacity-building? Mao Ning: At the 2026 World AI Conference & High-Level Meeting on Global AI Governance, President Xi Jinping announced that in the next five years, China will provide developing countries with 5,000 opportunities in AI training and seminar programs. To ensure its early implementation, China is hosting once again a Workshop on AI Capacity-Building in Peking University from September 7 to 12. As part of the continued efforts to implement the AI Capacity-Building Action Plan for Good and for All, China established the World Artificial Intelligence Cooperation Organization, in an effort to make relevant technologies and services more accessible, and help Global South countries find a path to AI development suited to their needs. We will work with various parties to make AI a lasting source of benefits and a major driving force for the welfare of all humanity. AFP: India is scheduled to host a BRICS summit this weekend. Can the foreign ministry confirm who will be attending on China’s behalf? Secondly, what are China’s expectations for this BRICS summit? Mao Ning: China sets great store by BRICS cooperation. We support India in hosting a successful BRICS summit this year. For your specific questions, I don’t have more information to offer at the moment. China Daily: It’s reported that Lai Ching-te claimed at an event that China is contorting UNGA Resolution 2758. Taiwan is a “sovereign independent nation.” The resolution only addresses the People’s Republic of China’s representation at the UN and has nothing to do with Taiwan. What is China’s comment on this? Mao Ning: There is but one China in the world, and Taiwan is an inalienable part of China’s territory. This is an unshakable fact grounded in both history and law. The Cairo Declaration issued by China, the U.S. and the UK in 1943 stated in explicit terms that Taiwan is a territory that Japan had stolen and shall be restored to China. The Potsdam Proclamation in 1945 reaffirmed that the terms of the Cairo Declaration shall be carried out. This series of instruments with legal effect under international law have all clearly affirmed China’s sovereignty over Taiwan. UNGA Resolution 2758 solemnly reaffirmed the one-China principle, which “decides to restore all its rights to the People’s Republic of China and to recognize the representatives of its Government as the only legitimate representatives of China to the United Nations.” From political, legal and procedural aspects, the resolution resolved once and for all the question of the representation of the whole of China, including Taiwan, in the UN. It made clear that there is only one seat of China in the United Nations, and there is no such thing as “two Chinas” or “one China, one Taiwan.” Taiwan has never been a country and will never be a country. The Lai Ching-te authorities’ deliberate distortion of UNGA Resolution 2758 once again revealed their separatist nature for “Taiwan independence.” Their rhetoric will not change the historical and legal fact that the two sides of the Taiwan Strait belong to one and the same China, nor will it undermine the international community’s steadfast commitment to one China.

item.title: Foreign Ministry Spokesperson Mao Ning’s Regular Press Conference on September 7, 2026
item.description:
Published: 2026-09-07
CGTN: We noted that a delegation from the Organisation for the Prohibition of Chemical Weapons (OPCW) visited China and inspected facilities for the disposal of Japan’s abandoned chemical weapons (ACWs). Could you please provide more information on the visit? Mao Ning: From August 31 to September 5, the Director-General of the OPCW, the Chairperson of the Executive Council, as well as permanent representatives and senior diplomats from 12 countries to the OPCW, visited China upon invitation. During the visit, they travelled to Hunchun, Dunhua and Haerbaling in Jilin Province to inspect the excavation, recovery and destruction of Japan’s ACWs. The delegation’s visit coincided with China’s annual commemoration of the victory of the Chinese People’s War of Resistance Against Japanese Aggression and the World Anti-Fascist War. Japan’s militarist aggression inflicted immense humanitarian catastrophes on China and left behind the menace of ACWs. Through the visit, the delegation gained a deeper understanding of the grave harm posed by Japan’s ACWs to the lives and property of the Chinese people and to the country’s ecological environment, and expressed support for the OPCW, in accordance with the Chemical Weapons Convention, in urging the Japanese side to earnestly fulfill its obligations by completely and thoroughly destroying its ACWs in China without further delay, so as to restore a safe habitat for the Chinese people at an early date and realize the noble goal of a world free of chemical weapons as envisaged by the Convention. Reuters: We spoke to the Philippines’ defense secretary earlier today and he said China could use recently scaled-down U.S.-South Korean military exercises as an opportunity to assert itself in the Indo-Pacific region. Do you have anything to say to that comment? Mao Ning: China is always committed to maintaining peace and stability in the Asia Pacific, and does not engage in major-country confrontation. We hope other regional countries will also play a positive role for peace and stability in the region. China News Service: According to the Solomon Star, Taiwan increased its annual aid to Palau from US$18 million last year to US$25 million this year, apparently in an effort to secure political backing at the Pacific Islands Forum. The Taiwan authorities also allocated nearly US$281,000 in direct cash gifts for Palau’s former president, incumbent political figures, and individual lawmakers. The report commented that Taiwan’s taxpayers’ hard-earned money is not being spent on people’s livelihoods. What’s your comment? Mao Ning: The report is yet another example of the Lai Ching-te authorities’ expensive dollar diplomacy using the hard-earned money of the people in Taiwan—a combination of corruption, fraudulence, bribery and power-for-money deals—to serve “Taiwan independence” separatism and their personal political agenda. For certain countries like Palau, having Taiwan as a “diplomatic ally” is not about delivering for the country and the people, but to line the pockets of the very few people who profit from it. EFE: Venezuela says its agreements with China will be respected and Chinese joint ventures will continue operating. Has Caracas given Beijing specific assurances that Chinese oil interests will not be affected by the new U.S.-Venezuela agreement? Mao Ning: Cooperation between China and Venezuela is under the protection of international law and laws of both countries. It has nothing to do with any third party and should not be disrupted by any third party. China’s lawful rights and interests in Venezuela must be protected. AFP: The United States and China will hold talks on AI safety risks in coming weeks. This is according to a recent report by Reuters. Can the foreign ministry confirm these talks? They will reportedly take place in mid-September. What are Chinese expectations for these discussions? Mao Ning: China and the U.S. maintain communication on AI. DPA: The far-right Alternative for Germany (AfD) won the election in the eastern state of Saxony-Anhalt. In an interview with Phoenix TV, the AfD lead candidate Ulrich Siegmund said that for Germany’s better development in the future, Germany needs China from a long-term perspective. What’s China’s take on this election result? Will China enhance communication with the AfD? Mao Ning: Regional elections in Germany are its domestic affair. China will not comment on that. China’s position on developing its relations with Germany is consistent. The Paper: We’ve learned that a group of foreign journalists were allowed by China to gain access to the disaster-hit area in Gyirong for interviews. Can you share more details on that? Mao Ning: The mudslide in Gyirong has drawn close attention from the international media, who hope to enter the area for reporting and interviews. With roads having just been cleared after non-stop repair work, China invited journalists from eight foreign media outlets, including the NBC, CNN, Reuters, RT and PTI, to enter the core area to learn about the impact of the disaster and progress in rescue, recovery and reconstruction. They also attended the group interview for journalists held by Xizang Autonomous Region. I believe you have seen the media reports from these outlets. China will continue its all-out search and rescue efforts to deal with the aftermath. We will provide timely updates on the situation on the ground and rescue operations.

item.title: Foreign Ministry Spokesperson Guo Jiakun’s Regular Press Conference on September 4, 2026
item.description:
Published: 2026-09-04
CNA: Singapore’s foreign ministry has just released a statement stating that 52 Singaporeans were arrested in Guangxi following a law enforcement operation against suspected pyramid scheme activities. Can we get China’s comment on this? What specific charges are those who have been arrested facing? Could you also share more details on the case and when the investigations begin? Guo Jiakun: China handles cases involving illegal or criminal activities by foreign nationals on Chinese soil in accordance with the law and ensures that their lawful rights are fully protected. I’d refer you to Chinese competent authorities for more information. Asahi Shimbun: Nicaraguan lawmakers on Tuesday approved a constitutional reform restricting the participation of opposition politicians in elections. The amendment also extended the presidential term. What’s China’s comment on that? As China is growing its relations with Nicaragua, how does China assess the current state and future prospects of bilateral relations? Guo Jiakun: China stays committed to the principle of non-interference in other countries’ internal affairs, and advocates that all countries’ right to follow development path that suits the national conditions should be respected. China will develop friendly ties with Nicaragua and other countries on the basis of mutual respect and win-win cooperation. CNA: Could I ask a follow-up on your response? What coordination has there been with Singaporean authorities on the matter? What next steps are being taken? Could you also confirm if this is part of a wider investigation into pyramid schemes and if other nationalities are involved? Guo Jiakun: I just shared information on the relevant question. For more specifics, I’d refer you to competent authorities. Reuters: U.S. Trade Representative Jamieson Greer said on Thursday that the two countries expected to make some announcements on agriculture and non-tariff barriers related to agriculture to incentivize American sales into China during the anticipated presidential summit in Washington later this month. Does the foreign ministry have any comment on these remarks? Guo Jiakun: On the specifics you mentioned, I have no information to share. China and the U.S. need to jointly deliver on the important common understandings between the two presidents, and maintain the steady growth momentum of China-U.S. economic and trade ties. Bloomberg: The leaders of the Pacific island nations have criticized China’s recent missile test, saying they didn’t get adequate notice. Would the ministry like to respond to this? The Pacific island nations called for giving at least 24 hours notice of such missile testing in the future. I wonder if China will commit to giving at least 24 hours notice for similar missile tests in the future? (Similar question from AFP) Guo Jiakun: China has on many occasions made clear its position on the test launch. China is committed to peaceful development and a national defense policy that is defensive in nature. We never engage in military expansion. China stands ready to work with South Pacific countries to contribute to peace, stability, development and prosperity of the South Pacific region.

item.title: Foreign Ministry Spokesperson Guo Jiakun’s Regular Press Conference on September 3, 2026
item.description:
Published: 2026-09-03
At the invitation of Member of the Political Bureau of the CPC Central Committee and Minister of Foreign Affairs Wang Yi, Secretary of Foreign Affairs of Mexico Roberto Velasco Álvarez will visit China from September 6 to 7. CCTV: Yesterday, President Xi Jinping successfully concluded his state visit to Egypt. Can you share more information about this visit? Guo Jiakun: This is President Xi Jinping’s first state visit to Egypt in 10 years. As this year marks the 70th anniversary of the establishment of China-Egypt diplomatic relations, the visit carries great significance in building on the past achievements and charting the future of our bilateral ties. During the visit, President Xi Jinping held talks with President El-Sisi and had an in-depth exchange of views on China-Egypt relations, bilateral cooperation across the board, and international and regional issues of mutual interest. President Xi pointed out that in recent years, the China-Egypt comprehensive strategic partnership has realized leapfrog development. Faced with the changing and turbulent international and regional situation, the two countries should support each other, deepen cooperation, and continue to build a China-Egypt community with a shared future. He emphasized that the two sides should firmly support each other, maintain the momentum of high-level exchanges, intensify exchanges and cooperation across different areas and levels, and strengthen the exchange and mutual learning of governance experience; the two sides should advance mutually beneficial cooperation, enhance synergy between development strategies, unleash cooperation potential in traditional areas, and foster new cooperation highlights in areas such as green energy; the two sides should promote people-to-people exchanges by expanding exchanges and cooperation across the board in areas such as culture and education, and increasing the flow of personnel, in order to boost connectivity between the two peoples; the two sides should strengthen security cooperation by jointly combating transnational crime, deepening international cooperation against corruption, and firmly supporting each other’s counter-terrorism efforts, so as to safeguard the two countries’ common security; and the two sides should enhance international and multilateral collaboration by coordinating and cooperating more closely at multilateral platforms such as the United Nations and BRICS, and jointly advancing the building of the China-Arab States Cooperation Forum and the Forum on China-Africa Cooperation, to oppose unilateralism and bullying acts together, and promote a more just and equitable global governance system. President Xi made a four-point proposal on improving the common security of the Middle East. First, unleashing the internal momentum of regional common security. The people in the Middle East should be the masters of their own affairs. Regional countries should be supported in strengthening dialogue on peace and security. Second, advancing the comprehensive governance of regional common security. The many highly interrelated hotspot issues in the Middle East require comprehensive solutions. Third, cementing the development foundation of regional common security. Lasting stability and security in the Middle East relies fundamentally on development. Fourth, enhancing international coordination on regional common security. The UN Charter and international law serve as the basic guidelines for handling Middle East affairs. The UN should be supported in playing a tangible role in regional affairs. After the talks, the two presidents jointly witnessed the signing of multiple cooperation documents in areas including Belt and Road cooperation, artificial intelligence, economy and trade, and industrial and supply chain cooperation. The two sides issued the Joint Statement on Deepening the China-Egypt Comprehensive Strategic Partnership. During the visit, the two sides also signed more than 20 cooperation documents in areas such as digital economy, science and technology, education, and transport. Pheonix TV: Yesterday, you said that China was preparing the third batch of relief supplies for Nepal. Could you share with us the latest progress? What cooperation has been carried out between China and Nepal on meteorological monitoring and disaster early-warning? Guo Jiakun: The third batch of emergency relief supplies from China to Nepal has been sent this morning, including tents, blankets, mortuary refrigerators, medical protective suit and satellite communication equipment. China also sent a second group of DNA forensic experts to assist Nepal. The Xizang Autonomous Region has sent two Bailey bridges to Nepal. The Red Cross Society of China and China Foundation for Rural Development donated emergency relief supplies to Nepal. Associations of overseas Chinese and Chinese companies in Nepal have also offered support and donations. China will continue to provide emergency assistance and conduct international search and rescue cooperation in light of Nepal’s needs. In the wake of the disaster, China’s meteorological, water resources and other authorities have conducted close cooperation with relevant Nepali authorities in sharing monitoring information and disaster response. The China Meteorological Administration (CMA) established immediate contact with the Department of Hydrology and Meteorology of Nepal. The two sides have held weather consultations via video link and shared information in real time. The CMA urgently developed a customized cloud edition of MAZU system and delivered it to Nepal for trial use to provide meteorological support for Nepal’s rescue and relief efforts. China’s Ministry of Water Resources has continuously shared with Nepal information on hydrological monitoring, early-warnings and forecasts. Nepal expressed deep appreciation to China for standing side by side with it in responding to the disaster and providing vital support for its relief efforts, and stated that this reflects the great friendship between the two neighbors. China will continue to enhance cooperation with Nepal in related areas and strongly support Nepal in its emergency rescue and relief efforts. Xinhua News Agency: You just announced the upcoming visit by Mexican Secretary of Foreign Affairs Roberto Velasco Álvarez. How does China view the current bilateral ties with Mexico? What does China expect from the visit? Guo Jiakun: Mexico is a major country in Latin America and an important emerging market. China and Mexico are comprehensive strategic partners. Over the past five decades since the establishment of diplomatic ties, China-Mexico relations have continued to develop in depth, with fruitful exchanges and cooperation across the board and close coordination and collaboration in international and regional affairs. The upcoming visit will mark Mr. Velasco’s first visit to China since he took office in April. Through the visit, China hopes that the two sides will have an in-depth exchange of views on bilateral relations and international and regional issues of common interest, further enhance political mutual trust, deepen mutually beneficial cooperation, promote the steady growth of China-Mexico relations, and deliver more benefits to both peoples. Reuters: Among the 21 dead already found on the Chinese side of the disaster so far, have their identifies been verified and are there foreign nationals among the deceased? Guo Jiakun: The authorities of the Xizang Autonomous Region shared relevant information at their press briefings. We will continue communicating and coordinating with relevant parties to properly verify their identities and handle follow-up matters. Global Times: The 2026 defense white paper recently issued by Japan’s Ministry of Defense (MoD) claimed that Japan will further seek “enemy base strike capability.” The MoD also requested a record 8.89 trillion yen for fiscal year 2027. Comments say that Japan is stepping up effort to break free from postwar pacifism, abandon the “exclusively defense-oriented” policy and seek offensive capability. But some say that Japan has the right to become a “normal country” and develop military strength. Today marks the 81st anniversary of the victory of the Chinese People’s War of Resistance Against Japanese Aggression and the World Anti-Fascist War. Do you think Japan is challenging the outcomes of WWII victory? How will China respond? Guo Jiakun: The designation of the Victory Day of the Chinese People’s War of Resistance Against Japanese Aggression is to remember the profound suffering that Japanese militarist aggression imposed on the people of China and the rest of the world, to remind the public not to forget history, and to uphold the outcomes of WWII victory and postwar international order. Over the years, Japanese right-wing forces have tried to turn the verdict on the history of aggression, and break free from the postwar international arrangements and their international obligations. It needs to be stressed that a series of international instruments including the Cairo Declaration, the Potsdam Proclamation and Japan’s Instrument of Surrender have affirmed in legal terms Japan’s status as a defeated state, and explicitly stipulated the obligations of defeated states, including eradicating militarism, abolishing military industries, dismantling war capability, and not rearming for war. These postwar international arrangements help uphold historical truth and international justice, set up an institutional line of defense against the resurrection of militarism, and embody the outcomes of the victory of the World Anti-Fascist War. Our solemn message to Japanese right-wing forces: the right way forward for Japan is to fulfill its international obligations, fully remove the pernicious influence of militarism, and keep to peaceful development. China will stand together with peace-loving countries in the world to firmly hold back the malevolent emergence of Japanese neo-militarism under the pretext of making Japan a “normal country,” and prevent it from wreaking havoc to the region and beyond. Bloomberg: Some in Nepal are demanding climate compensation from the world’s biggest emitters of greenhouse gases. This would be the U.S., India and China. This comes after the deadly flood that killed many people. Would the foreign ministry like to comment? Guo Jiakun: Climate change is a global challenge that requires the collective efforts of all parties. China has been a steadfast actor and major contributor in promoting global green development. We are making active and sound efforts towards the carbon peak and neutrality goals and expected to make the world’s biggest cut in carbon emission intensity. As the largest developing country, China firmly upholds the legitimate and lawful rights and interests of the developing world, strives for a fair and equitable global climate governance system for win-win cooperation, and provides assistance to other developing countries to the best of its capability via South-South cooperation. China and Nepal are a community with a shared future linked by mountains and rivers. And China is also severely affected by this cross-border disaster. We are ready to strengthen cooperation with Nepal and the rest of the international community to jointly prevent and mitigate the negative impact of climate change. NHK: The Japan-China Friendship Parliamentarians’ Union is reportedly considering sending a delegation to China this month, which consists of young lawmakers from both the ruling and opposition parties. How does the Chinese side view this initiative and what’s your expectation？ Guo Jiakun: Some visionary people in Japan are deeply concerned over the current state of China-Japan relations and wish to make an effort to improve bilateral ties. We are ready to engage with them in the hope of enhancing mutual understanding and trust as long as they abide by the four political documents, support a friendly China policy, and cherish China-Japan relations. We call on those running the government of Japan to listen to and value the voice of reason at home and create the conditions necessary for normal exchanges between China and Japan with concrete actions. Reuters: The president of Palau and current chair of the regional Pacific Islands Forum said today he was hoping to gain consensus from member nations to condemn a Chinese missile test recently held in the region. What is the foreign ministry’s comment? Guo Jiakun: China has more than once made clear its position on the test launch. Palau has repeatedly raised this issue in an ill-intentioned attempt to hijack the position of other member states of the Pacific Islands Forum. It will not have its way. China is committed to peaceful development and a national defense policy that is defensive in nature. We never engage in military expansion. China stands ready to work with South Pacific countries to contribute to peace, stability, development and prosperity of the South Pacific region. Bloomberg: U.S. Energy Secretary Chris Wright has said that China won’t have any debt claims to the revenue from new oil production in Venezuela. If this happens, can you provide more details of how China might protect its interests in Venezuela? Does China feel like it can rely on international law to protect its interests in this case? Finally, are you worried at all that the U.S. attitude on oil and Venezuela might set a precedent and encourage Washington to seize Chinese assets in Latin America or elsewhere? Guo Jiakun: China-Venezuela cooperation is protected by international law and laws of both countries. The cooperation does not concern any third party and should not be subjected to interference by any third party. China’s lawful rights and interests in Venezuela must be protected. Shenzhen TV: Viet Nam’s foreign ministry spokesperson reportedly said in a recent statement that Viet Nam has sovereignty over the Paracels and reiterated that “all foreign activities in the Paracel Islands, including at Ba Ba Island and at Hai Sam Reef, conducted without Viet Nam’s permission are completely illegal, null and void.” The country has made serious representations and demands an immediate end to such activities and that they not be repeated, she added. What’s China’s comment on this? Guo Jiakun: Xisha Qundao is China’s territory without any dispute. It is within China’s sovereign rights to conduct necessary construction on its own territory. There is no room for unwarranted accusations from Viet Nam. AFP: The coast guard of Taiwan said today that it deployed vessels to monitor two Chinese ships operating in waters to its east, saying it firmly rejects China’s campaign of “law enforcement in name, jurisdictional expansion in practice.” Does the Chinese foreign ministry have a reaction to this? Guo Jiakun: This is not a question about foreign affairs. ************************************************** The following question was raised after the press conference: The Chinese exhibition team announced it will withdraw from the Gwangju Biennale in the ROK in strong protest against the organizer’s wrongful practice related to Taiwan. The Chinese embassy in the ROK has made a statement on that. What’s your comment? Guo Jiakun: The China-ROK joint communiqué on the establishment of diplomatic relations states clearly that “the government of the Republic of Korea recognizes the government of the People’s Republic of China as the sole legal government of China and respects China’s position that there is only one China and Taiwan is part of China.” The ROK side also clearly stated on many occasions this year that its commitment to the one-China position remains unchanged. The organizer of the ROK Gwangju Biennale, however, has stubbornly clung to the wrongful practice, allowing China’s Taiwan region to participate under a designation that is completely incompatible with its status. This is a grave violation of the one-China principle. China is firmly opposed to this and has lodged serious representations with the ROK side, demanding that the relevant party immediately correct its wrongdoings. We hope that the ROK government will honor its political commitments, earnestly shoulder its responsibilities, and uphold the one-China principle with concrete actions. It’s despicable for the DPP authorities to exploit occasions such as cultural exchanges, conferences and exhibitions to engage in political manipulation and make “Taiwan independence” provocations. Their political schemes are doomed to fail.

item.title: Foreign Ministry Spokesperson Guo Jiakun’s Regular Press Conference on September 2, 2026
item.description:
Published: 2026-09-02
People’s Daily: This year marks the 25th anniversary of the Shanghai Cooperation Organization. Yesterday, President Xi Jinping attended in Bishkek the 26th meeting of the Council of Heads of State of the SCO and the SCO Plus Meeting. Could you please provide more information on this? Guo Jiakun: On September 1, President Xi Jinping attended the 26th meeting of the Council of Heads of State of the Shanghai Cooperation Organization and delivered important remarks titled “Toward Higher Quality Development of the Shanghai Cooperation Organization.” President Xi pointed out that over the past 25 years, the SCO has traveled an extraordinary journey. Its biggest achievement is that it has steadily grown into a new type of regional cooperation organization with the largest land area and population and enormous development potential. Its most valuable spiritual asset is that it pioneered, and has since followed invariably, the Shanghai Spirit of mutual trust, mutual benefit, equality, consultation, respect for diversity of civilizations, and pursuit of common development. Its most important experience for cooperation is that it has found the right way of coexistence featuring non-alliance, non-confrontation and not targeting any third party, enabling regional countries to build a common home together. President Xi put forward four points for the SCO’s future development, namely, staying committed to putting development first and opening up the prospects for shared prosperity, staying committed to taking security as a key goal and fostering an environment of common security, staying committed to a people-centered approach and cementing the foundation for everlasting friendship, and staying committed to dialogue and consultation and striving for more equitable and orderly governance. President Xi stressed that China will work with all parties to continue to hold high the banner of the Shanghai Spirit, implement the development strategy of the SCO for the next decade, and pursue development with higher quality, so as to make greater contributions to a community with a shared future for humanity. On the same day, President Xi attended the SCO Plus Meeting and delivered an important statement titled “Jointly Advocating an Equal and Orderly Multipolar World and Making Global Governance More Just and Equitable.” In his remarks, President Xi provided a profound analysis on questions such as what kind of multipolarity the world needs and how countries and the SCO are going to take part in and promote an equal and orderly multipolar world. He proposed three points on better leveraging the role of the SCO, namely, advancing common prosperity in the vast continent straddling Asia and Europe with the SCO Strength, promoting the development and rise of the Global South through the SCO Wisdom, and guiding the reform and improvement of global governance through the SCO Action. President Xi stressed that a more united and vibrant SCO is fully capable of making greater contributions to a multipolar world. All parties expressed appreciation for China’s important contribution to the organization’s development as a founding member, and agreed to actively implement the strategic vision set out at the 2025 Tianjin Summit, continue to uphold the Shanghai Spirit, promote institution-building, enhance political mutual trust, deepen cooperation in various areas, strengthen people-to-people bonds, and jointly respond to new types of security challenges, with a view to writing a new chapter of lasting peace and common development. Pheonix TV: We have learned that the Second Meeting of G20 Finance Ministers and Central Bank Governors held from August 31 to September 1 failed to issue a communiqué due to China’s differing view on global imbalances. Would you like to comment on this? Guo Jiakun: As an important member of the G20, China places high emphasis on the organization’s role as the premier forum for international economic cooperation. Since the United States assumed the 2026 presidency of the G20, the Chinese side has participated in relevant discussions including along the Finance Track in an active and constructive manner and contributed to practical outcomes under various mechanisms. We have noted that parties hold diverging views on certain issues at the recent Meeting of G20 Finance Ministers and Central Bank Governors. We regret that the meeting failed to issue a communiqué. The G20, as the premier platform for global economic cooperation, should play its coordinating role on key issues concerning the global economy in an objective, impartial and balanced manner based on the principle of consensus through consultation and equal participation. We hope the United States in its presidency and other members will abide by this principle, give full respect to all parties’ legitimate concerns, and strive for a fruitful Miami Summit. China stands ready to work with the United States to act on the important common understandings reached between the two presidents and join hands with fellow members to enable the G20 to play a positive role in deepening macroeconomic policy coordination, improving global economic governance, and boosting world economic growth. The Paper: It was reported that the second batch of relief supplies provided by China has been delivered to the Nepalese side yesterday. Can you share more details? Can you also update us on what China has done on sharing information about foreign nationals who remain unaccounted for? Guo Jiakun: The second batch of emergency relief supplies provided by China to Nepal arrived in Kathmandu yesterday afternoon. Five DNA forensic experts were also on the plane to assist Nepal in their operations. The Nepalese side thanked China for urgently sending more supplies and providing technical support. China is preparing the third batch of emergency relief supplies based on the request of Nepal. These supplies will include Bailey bridges, mortuary refrigerators, epidemic prevention supplies and emergency communication equipment. China will also send a second group of DNA experts. In the wake of the disaster, China has kept close communication with relevant countries’ embassies in China to jointly identify missing personnel and properly handle follow-up matters. As we speak, residents of the border areas and pilgrims who were previously stranded in the disaster-hit areas are leaving China via land or air transportation in an orderly manner. Yesterday, the foreign ministry briefed relevant foreign embassies in China on the missing foreign nationals. China will continue to keep the channel of communication with relevant embassies unimpeded by various means. China attaches great importance to the safety of Chinese nationals and institutions in Nepal. We are working with Nepal to make all-out effort to search for and rescue missing Chinese nationals, and assisting the relocation of many Chinese nationals to safety. The Chinese embassy in Nepal will continue to do all we can to assist Chinese nationals in need. AFP: Can the Chinese foreign ministry please provide an updated toll of those who are still missing from the mudslide disaster? Are there new figures since Sunday? And specifically, how many foreigners are missing on the Chinese side? What is the breakdown of their nationalities? How many Chinese citizens are among the dead in Nepal and how many Chinese citizens remain missing in Nepal? Guo Jiakun: The authorities of the Xizang Autonomous Region shared detailed information at the recent press briefing. Yesterday the foreign ministry also informed relevant countries’ embassies in China. According to the latest information, a total of 261 foreign nationals from 23 countries are among those missing. We will continue communicating and coordinating with relevant parties to jointly identify missing persons and properly handle follow-up matters. Nearly 100 Chinese nationals remain unaccounted for in Nepal. We thank the Nepali side for rescuing and transferring Chinese nationals in Nepal and hope these efforts will continue. Ukrinform News Agency: Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelensky said that Ukraine will intensify deep strikes on military facilities within the Russian territory, which is why the airspace of Russia became dangerous. He has instructed the Ukrainian foreign ministry to inform other countries about the danger of flying in Russian airspace. Chinese airlines companies continue to use Russian skies for passenger and other flights. I’d like to ask whether the foreign ministry has already received a warning from the Ukrainian side and will China respond to the increasing danger？ Guo Jiakun: Dialogue and negotiation is the only viable way out of the Ukraine crisis. We urge the parties concerned to remain calm and exercise restraint, jointly work toward early deescalation and accumulate conditions for the political settlement of the crisis. Asahi Shimbun: Iranian media reported that the Chinese and Iranian leaders had a brief conversation during the SCO Bishkek summit. Can you confirm that? What topics did they discuss? Guo Jiakun: We have released information on President Xi Jinping’s participation in the SCO Bishkek summit, during which he had cordial exchanges with leaders of various countries. Bloomberg: The Russian president and the Chinese leader reportedly discussed holding a trilateral meeting with the U.S. president. That would be when China hosts the APEC summit later this year. Would the foreign ministry like to comment on that? Guo Jiakun: On this question, I have no information to share at the moment. As the host for this year’s APEC, China stands ready to work with all parties for the full success of the APEC China Year and make new contribution to the economic growth of the Asia Pacific and beyond. Beijing Daily: Recently, Mr. Ronald Sakolsky returned to China for the first time in 27 years and was reunited with Ms. Yin Yuzhen, a national model worker and renowned figure in China’s fight against desertification. Their moving story has attracted widespread attention. What is your comment? Guo Jiakun: Recently, our American friend Mr. Ronald Sakolsky, affectionately known in China as “Saikaosi” for supporting China’s fight against desertification, visited China upon invitation after 27 years. During his visit, Mr. Sakolsky traveled to Inner Mongolia, where he joined Ms. Yin Yuzhen, a national model worker, and revisited the forest he helped fund years ago, and together planted a tree of friendship. He also returned to the school in Luoyang, Henan Province, where he once taught, to meet with teachers and students. He visited Beijing as well. Throughout his visit, Mr. Sakolsky witnessed firsthand the remarkable changes that have taken place in China and once again experienced the warmth and hospitality of the Chinese people. He was deeply moved and shed tears on several occasions. I noted that in an interview with the media, Mr. Sakolsky said that Ms. Yin and he have shown that they can bridge cultures and break down boundaries. He said that the American and Chinese people both want to live in peace. China and the United States are like two roads, they may take different routes, but they can still lead to the same destination. His sincere words have touched many people. They reflect a shared aspiration of the people of both countries. The hope of the China-U.S. relationship lies in the people, and its foundation lies in grassroots connections. The many inspiring stories written together by the Chinese and American people are a vivid testament to our people-to-people friendship. They also once again demonstrate that China and the United States, as two major countries, can achieve mutual success, and contribute to the well-being of the world. China will, as always, support more visits and exchanges between the two peoples, so that we can continue to write new chapters in our people-to-people friendship and make greater contributions to the development of China-U.S. relations. Global Times: Eighty one years ago today, Japan officially signed the Instrument of Surrender, marking the ultimate triumph of the global fight against fascism. We notice that MFA spokesperson has shared China’s views on the “Enemy State Clauses.” But some believe that there’s no longer an “enemy state” in the world anymore. The “Enemy State Clauses” have expired and are no longer relevant. What’s your take on that? Can you give us more information on China’s position? Guo Jiakun: On September 2, 1945, the Japanese government officially signed the Instrument of Surrender, and accepted all the terms of the Potsdam Proclamation, establishing the undeniable historical conclusion that the war waged by Japan’s militarists was for aggression. It is also a part of the postwar international order that shall not be challenged. The “Enemy State Clauses” are still in the UN Charter and consist of Article 53, 77 and 107. It is a special set of rules for defeated states, aiming to prevent them from threatening international peace and security once again, and has provided important institutional safeguards for defending postwar international order. Japan joined the UN after recognizing its militarist crimes and accepting the UN Charter in its entirety. Today, however, those running the Japanese government keep sidestepping the issue of historical crimes, and even go to great lengths to distort and whitewash its crimes of aggression and move faster to remilitarize Japan. They continue to pay tribute to Class-A war criminals in WWII and attempt to revise the pacifist Constitution. What’s worse, Japan’s ties with nearly all its neighbors have witnessed increased tension. Japan blatantly interferes in the internal affairs of other countries, and even threatens to use force. The “gray rhino” of Japan’s neo-militarism is charging towards us, and posing a threat to peace and stability in the Asia Pacific once again. Against such backdrop, it is extremely necessary to reaffirm the commitment to the UN Charter, in particular, the “Enemy State Clauses.” We urge the Japanese government to earnestly abide by its international obligations stipulated by the Instrument of Surrender, face up to and learn lessons from history, make a clean break with militarism, and earn the trust of its Asian neighbors and the rest of the world with concrete actions. PTI: Reports say that the high-altitude Himalayan region is warming significantly, faster than the global average. Studies have shown since 1981, the Qinghai-Tibet Plateau have lost roughly 20 percent of its glaciers attributed to the climate change crisis. In the light of the August 26 glacier collapse, how does China view the glacier retreat crisis impacting the Himalayan region and the calls for formation of a coordination mechanism by China with neighbouring countries, to strengthen cooperation to deal with such disasters affecting the fragile region? Guo Jiakun: China has responded to similar questions. According to the assessment of Chinese and Nepali experts, long-term effects of global warming have made glaciers unstable, and this disaster was triggered by the collapse of a glacier in Nepal, resulting in a rapid crash of ice and rocks which took away a chunk of the mountain. The Xizang Autonomous Region shared relevant information at its press conference. China and Nepal have maintained sound cooperation in meteorology, water conservancy and disaster prevention and reduction. In the wake of the disaster, China has shared with Nepal important information such as images, satellite, and hydrological data of the disaster-affected areas, including early-warning information on an upstream barrier lake. We will continue to give strong support to Nepal in its relief efforts and strengthen cooperation on disaster prevention and reduction. Climate change is a common challenge facing all humanity. No country can stay immune from such risks. China will continue to work with the international community to strengthen exchanges and cooperation and effectively prevent and mitigate the negative impact of climate change. As for your specific question, I’d refer you to competent authorities. AFP: I wonder if China has been told if any Chinese citizens were among the dead in Nepal from the disaster last week? And also are you able to provide a specific figure on the number of Chinese nationals missing in China? Guo Jiakun: I just shared the information we have. As we speak, intensive rescue and relief operations are still underway. For the specific information you asked for, there will be continued updates.

item.title: Foreign Ministry Spokesperson’s Remarks on Japanese Politicians Paying Respects to the Yasukuni War Shrine Which Honors Class-A War Criminals
item.description:
Published: 2026-08-15
Q: August 15 marks the day of Japan’s unconditional surrender in the Second World War. Prime Minister of Japan Sanae Takaichi made a monetary offering to the Yasukuni war shrine today, and certain cabinet members also visited the shrine. What’s your comment? A: China strongly deplores Japan’s negative moves related to the Yasukuni war shrine, and has lodged serious protests against Japan. During WWII, Japan launched the war of aggression and committed horrendous crimes. The Yasukuni war shrine is a spiritual tool and symbol of Japanese militarism. It is in fact a shrine for war criminals, as it honors 14 convicted Class-A war criminals responsible for the war of aggression. No pretext whatsoever can hide the Japanese politicians’ true intention which is to change the verdict on the war criminals, cover up Japan’s war crimes, distort the historical facts, and pave the way for accelerating remilitarization. This is an affront to historical justice, a challenge to the foundational norms of civilization, and a provocation against the postwar international order. Such behaviors have been firmly rejected by the overwhelming majority of the international community. This year marks the 80th anniversary of the opening of the Tokyo Trials. To view and treat history correctly is an important prerequisite for Japan’s postwar return to the international community, the political foundation for Japan’s ties with neighboring countries, and more importantly, a key measure for Japan’s commitment to peaceful development. We urge the Japanese side to do serious soul-searching on its history of aggression, make a clean break with militarism, and earn trust from its Asian neighbors and the rest of the world with concrete actions.
